newsitem.title: BURMA: Suu Kyi kept at home, Burmese students bristle.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi kept at home, Burmese students bristle.

text.p: Burma's military rulers confined opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi to her home while student demonstrators attempted to stage another rally at the troubled Yangon Institute of Technology (YIT) on Wednesday.

A Suu Kyi aide told Reuters by telephone that the Nobel laureate had been told to remain inside her lakeside Rangoon home. Access to her house had been barred, the aide said, and no reasons were given for the action.
"It is virtual house arrest. We were informed yesterday that she cannot leave her compound..." the aide said.
Asked if restrictions on Suu Kyi may have been linked to the student protests, the aide said it was possible.
Diplomats said Suu Kyi's confinement could be temporary and was aimed at preventing her from becoming drawn unknowingly into any student unrest.
Spokesmen for the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) were not available for comment.
The restriction imposed on Suu Kyi by the SLORC followed student protests that began at the YIT late on Monday and culminated in the heart of the capital before sunrise on Tuesday.
Police detained about 300 of 400 student demonstrators near the central Shwe Dagon pagoda after they refused to disperse in the early hours of Tuesday.

The demonstration, which drew nearly 2,000 students at its peak on Monday, was the biggest street protest seen in Rangoon since the September 1988 pro-democracy uprisings in which thousands were killed or jailed by the SLORC.
YIT campus sources said about 50 Burmese students released by police after being held for demonstrating in the capital, planned to rally at the YIT later on Wednesday.
However, the students were persuaded by YIT lecturers to return to their classes and it was unknown if the rally would be staged as planned, the sources said.

They said the group was among the 300 students detained by police on Tuesday who were were protesting against police handling of a brawl between some of their colleagues and restaurant owners in October.
A SLORC spokesman said on Tuesday that most of the detained students had been released after their papers were checked to determine if they were "real students or infiltrators". He gave no numbers.
The YIT campus was calm, with regular traffic movement, but security personnel were checking the identities of those entering.
State-run newspapers, in commentaries on Wednesday, advised students to focus on their studies instead of associating themselves with dissident politicians.
Although they did not name the politicians, they were apparently referring to members of Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD), which is involved in a standoff with the SLORC.

The human rights group Amnesty International said in a statement that five members of the NLD's youth wing had been detained by the military for interrogation after they left Suu Kyi's house on Tuesday. "The compound is now sealed and no one can enter or leave," Amnesty said.
